title: Vertical alveolar bone augmentation of atrophied posterior mandibular regions with simultaneous dental implant placement using allogeneic bone rings vs autogenous bone rings: a randomized controlled clinical trial Ragab
authors: Mahmoud AE, Mohammad Yassin S, Ali Hassan S, Sayed Abdelmoneim H. Quintessence Int. 2024;55(3):232-243. doi:10.3290/j.qi.b4867849
supports: Clinical study from the botiss maxgraft bonering (processed human allograft) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Allogeneic bone rings can be a viable alternative to autogenous bone rings in augmenting the posterior aspect of the mandible, mitigating the concerns associated with donor site complications” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
